newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money dives on extra liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money dives on extra liquidity.

text.p: Dutch call money rates sank on Tuesday as extra liquidity flowed into the market, dealers said.
"The extra inflow of liquidity was very miscellaneous," said one dealer, adding it was due partly to the payment of student grants and civil servants' salaries.
Call money rates were quoted at 2.00 percent bid, down from 2.75-2.81 percent bid on Monday. dealers said most trades were done at about 2.25 percent bid.
"Trade in call money is quite hectic," said one dealer, adding there was some business in short-dated deposits as well.
Deposits were bid at a slightly higher level with one-month deposits bid at 2.72 percent and three-month paper also trading at 2.72 percent bid.
The weakening of the guilder against the mark had no impact on the market, said one dealer. The guilder was trading at 112.135 per 100 marks from 112.105 on Monday.

The outcome of today's U.S. Fed meeting was not worrying the market. "We expect a 25 basis point rise of the discount rate," said one dealer, adding it would not have much effect in the money market if it turned out to be 50 basis points.
"If it is a larger increase than 25 basis points it will not disturb the Dutch money market as such," he said, adding however that a temporary shakeout could not be ruled out.
